content.text:
Verifier is running the full journey suite on Track A. Summary of the two `ui-review` rounds, which materially changed the fix:

| Round | Finding | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reserve on the page container de-centred the hero heading 8px | Moved to a wrapper around the card; `h1Offset` back to 0 |
| 1 | Guard allowed `gap >= 0`, but the focus ring reaches past the button | Replaced the number with a measurement of the ring box |
| 2 | Ring read mid-`transition-all` — got the initial `3px/0px`, not the settled `2px/2px` | Poll until two consecutive samples agree |
| 2 | Card was 16/32 asymmetric under a full-width centred subtitle | Symmetric `px-4`; measured free — same gap, same doc heights, same submit position |

The second round's finding was the sharpest: my guard was reading the CSS *initial* outline values, which are 1px **looser** than the real ring — so a `gap=3` layout would have shipped with the focus indicator painted under the launcher. I verified the fix closes exactly that window by rebuilding at an 11px inset: five assertions pass, including every hit-target check, and only the settled ring guard catches it.

Also worth recording: `ui-review` retracted its own earlier claim that `element.focus()` doesn't satisfy Chromium's `:focus-visible`, confirming my measurement contradicted it. Both of us were wrong about something in this change and both corrections came from measuring rather than reasoning.

input.prompt:
Review branch `fix/286-launcher-safe-column` in /home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/contoso — the branch diff against `origin/main` (57d1bbf) plus every staged, unstaged and untracked file. Step 8 of the root AGENTS.md workflow.

**Classify each finding as a defect or a refinement.** The loop ends on a round with no defects, so I need that split explicitly.

## The change

Issue #286: the `fixed` chat launcher overlapped `/contact`'s submit button at phone widths. Measured at 390x844, the button rendered at x 48..342 against a launcher at 334..374 — an 8x32 overlap in which `document.elementFromPoint` returns the launcher, so the last 8px of the page's primary action opened the chat instead of submitting.

- `apps/web/src/lib/control-classes.ts` — new export `LAUNCHER_SAFE_COLUMN = 'max-sm:px-4'`, with a long derivation comment.
- `apps/web/src/app/contact/page.tsx` — wraps `<ContactForm />` in `<div className={\`flex w-full justify-center ${LAUNCHER_SAFE_COLUMN}\`}>`.
- `apps/web/e2e/launcher-safe-area.spec.ts` — new journey spec, 7 tests, untracked.

## Why the shape is what it is, so you can attack the reasoning rather than rediscover it

The issue proposed bottom padding on `main`. That cannot work: the launcher is `fixed`, so the page scrolls under it and every row passes through its band — a gutter separates them only at the document end, and `padding-bottom` moves nothing at `scrollY=0`. Horizontal separation is the only geometry that holds. My first sweep sampled only the document end and reported every route clean, which is the position where this defect cannot appear.

The reserve is 32px of total card inset (page `px-4` 16 + wrapper `px-4` 16), not the launcher's full 56px footprint, because past 32px the card narrows enough to wrap taller and the extra 28px of document pushes the submit button further below the fold — which is #286's *second* complaint. The lower bound is the focus ring, not the hit target: `ACTION_FOCUS` is `outline-2 outline-offset-2`, so the ring reaches 4px past the button and a 24px inset clears the tap target while painting the ring under the launcher.

## What I most want checked

1. **The spec is most of the diff.** Is it measuring what it claims? `tests/scripts/AGENTS.md` fixture rules do not apply here, but the root AGENTS.md rule about guards measuring effective behaviour rather than a nearby declaration very much does — that file's own examples are about `ring-0`, blurred shadows and `outlineWidth` reporting a UA default. One test reads computed `padding-right` at 639 and 640 to pin the breakpoint scoping; tell me if that crosses from "measuring the rendered result" into "measuring the declaration".
2. `flex w-full justify-center` on the new wrapper — the form is `w-full max-w-lg` and used to be centred by the parent's `items-center`. Verified centred at 834 and 1440 (gutters 161/161 and 464/464), but tell me if there is a width or a state where that wrapper changes layout in a way I have not measured.
3. Whether the constant belongs in `control-classes.ts` at all. That file's header describes itself as being about what controls share — boundaries and focus indicators — and this is a layout reservation. It is exported and documented there because it is a shared control-adjacent class constant, but I am not certain it is the right home.
4. The comment is long even by this file's standards. Say if any of it is wrong, unverifiable, or asserting something nothing measures — this repository has a written history of prose that asserted what nothing verified, and I would rather cut it than ship it.

## Process record

Two `ui-review` rounds and two `verifier` rounds ran.

- ui-review round 1: the reserve was on the page's outer container and de-centred the `Get in Touch` heading by 8px; moved to the card wrapper. And the guard permitted `gap >= 0` where the focus ring needs 4 more; replaced the number with a measurement of the ring box.
- ui-review round 2: the ring was being read mid-`transition-all`, returning the CSS initial `3px/0px` instead of the settled `2px/2px` — 1px looser, in the direction that lets a defect through. Fixed by polling until two consecutive samples agree. Also proposed symmetric insets over `pr-4` alone, measured free, which I took.
- verifier round 2: no test covered the `sm` boundary, so dropping the `max-sm:` prefix would pass everything. Added the seventh test.

Every assertion has been demonstrated against a deliberate break, including an 11px inset producing `gap=3` where the old transient reading passed at `ringGap=0` and the settled reading correctly fails at `-1`.

Final verifier state: `make -C apps/web ci` passes (lint, both type-checks, 175 unit tests, production build), full journey suite 143 passed, merges cleanly onto `origin/main`.

## Filed rather than fixed here — do not re-report as defects in this diff

- #334 — every catalogue and home product card sits under the launcher at every viewport. A standing decision; `chat-launcher.spec.ts` records that "covering content is tolerable".
- #326 — `/contact`'s submission error is not announced, and `isSubmitting` blurs the button so focus lands on `<body>`.
- #217, #218, #176 — other `/contact` defects. Confirmed unchanged by this diff (card backdrop samples identical before and after).
- The submit button remains ~4px below the fold at 390x844 at landing. Pre-existing; the differential test proves this change does not add to it.

Tell me if you think any of those actually blocks this change.

`code-review` found a genuine **defect**, and it was mine — the kind this repo has a written history of.

My comment's sweep table was measured on the page-column version and carried across unchanged when the reserve moved to the card wrapper. The claim is now verified rather than asserted.
- The reviewer's own arithmetic was slightly off too (560px vs the measured 592px content box); I used the measured figure.

git commit -F - <<'MSG'
fix(web): keep the chat launcher off the contact form's controls

The launcher is `fixed bottom-0 right-0` with `mr-4 mb-4` below `sm`, so it
owns the rightmost 56px of the viewport on every route. On /contact that
landed on the submit button: measured at 390x844 the button rendered at
48..342 against a launcher at 334..374, and `document.elementFromPoint`
returned the launcher over the last 8px of the page's only primary action.
A tap there opened the chat instead of submitting. The message textarea is
hit too at 360x740, by 8x40.

/contact now reserves the launcher's column around its card, via a shared
LAUNCHER_SAFE_COLUMN constant. Controls clear by 8px at every phone width
and their focus rings by 4px.

#286 proposed bottom padding on `main` and that cannot work. The launcher
is fixed, so the page scrolls under it and every row passes through its
band; a gutter separates them only at the document end, and padding-bottom
moves nothing already rendered at scrollY=0. Horizontal separation is the
only geometry that holds. The issue's sweep is also why the reserve is
opt-in: every catalogue product card sits under the launcher at every
viewport, which chat-launcher.spec.ts already records as tolerable, so
that stays as measured in #334 rather than changed here.

The value is 32px of total inset, not the launcher's full 56. The lower
bound is the focus ring rather than the hit target -- ACTION_FOCUS reaches
4px past the button, so a 24px inset clears the tap target and still paints
the ring under the launcher. The upper bound is width given up for nothing:
at 56px the submit is 214px on a 390px viewport, which the spec's floor
rejects.

Seven assertions, each demonstrated against a deliberate break: the
original defect for the three overlap checks, an unprefixed reserve for the
breakpoint scoping, a 160px reserve for both width and height bounds, a
24px and an 11px inset for the focus ring, and bogus selectors, a forced
`outline-style: none` and an above-sm viewport for the vacuity guards.

Two rounds of ui-review and one of code-review changed the shape rather
than confirming it, and all three findings are recorded because each was
a way the change looked finished and was not:

- The reserve first sat on the page container, which de-centred the hero
  heading 8px. It belongs on the card.
- The ring guard first read `getComputedStyle` immediately after Tab,
  returning the transition's initial 3px/0px rather than the settled
  2px/2px -- 1px looser, in the direction that lets a defect through. An
  11px inset produces gap=3, which the transient reading scored as
  clearing and the settled one correctly rejects.
- The comment's sweep table was measured on the page-container version and
  carried across unchanged. On this lever document height is flat from
  16px to 56px; the 28px cliff it claimed belongs to the rejected
  placement, and its cause was the subtitle wrapping, not the card.

Disputed and checked rather than complied with: ui-review reported that
`element.focus()` does not satisfy Chromium's `:focus-visible`. Measured
here it does -- outlineStyle solid, outlineWidth 2px -- matching what #148
records about programmatic focus on the drawer panel. ui-review confirmed
the correction. The guard uses Tab regardless, so nothing rests on it.

Filed rather than fixed: #334, #338, #339. #327 closed as a duplicate.

Closes #286
